correctness.rationale: Munn element is a birooted finite Cayley subtree; every minimal representing walk crosses its s-t path edges once and all other edges twice, giving length 2m-dist(s,t). Independent excursion-order choices at each vertex yield N_T(s,s)=d_s! product_{v!=s}(d_v-1)! and N_T(s,t)=product_internal(d_v-2)! product_other(d_v-1)! for distinct endpoints; labels of departing signed edges separate word choices. The fixed-tree maximum is max_degree times product (d_v-1)!. In rank two, with counts A,B,C of degree4,3,2, the handshake identity 3A+2B+C=m-1 maximizes 4*6^A*2^B by using A=floor((m-1)/3), then at most one degree3/degree2 depending on residue. Every admissible degree sequence embeds in the Cayley tree. Independent integer exact optimization over every degree count through m=31 reproduced unique profiles and M_m; finite tree and word enumeration checker was inspected but not re-executed completely.
residual_risks: Tree multiplicities count geodesic representing WORDS for a fixed element, not distinct elements or arbitrary lengths.
Small word enumeration does not prove the all-m statement; the combinatorial bijection and integer optimization do.

These are motivated complete extremal classifications not evident from previously known length or element-growth formulas.
